1	# Scientific method note
2	
3	This task uses the scientific meaning of empirical dispersion corrections in
4	density-functional calculations and the package-independent data model used
5	by cclib. The note is a compact offline reference, not a copy of the upstream
6	bug report or its patch.
7	
8	## Method evidence
9	
10	The primary method reference is:
11	
12	> S. Grimme, J. Antony, S. Ehrlich, H. Krieg, “A consistent and accurate ab
13	> initio parametrization of density functional dispersion correction (DFT-D)
14	> for the 94 elements H-Pu,” *The Journal of Chemical Physics* 132, 154104
15	> (2010). DOI: [10.1063/1.3382344](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3382344).
16	
17	The software/data-model reference is:
18	
19	> N. M. O'Boyle et al., “cclib: A library for package-independent
20	> computational chemistry algorithms,” *Journal of Computational Chemistry*
21	> 29, 839-845 (2008). DOI:
22	> [10.1002/jcc.20823](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcc.20823).
23	
24	The source snapshot contains the package's BSD-3-Clause license and its
25	documentation. The method paper and the source documentation are the
26	authoritative offline materials for this task.
27	
28	## Energy meaning
29	
30	An empirical dispersion model supplements a density-functional energy with a
31	signed pairwise contribution. In a simplified notation,
32	
33	```text
34	E_method = E_base + E_pairwise
35	```
36	
37	where the pairwise term is built from atom-pair coefficients, interatomic
38	distances, and a damping function. A representative form is
39	
40	```text
41	E_pairwise = - sum(A < B) sum(n) s_n C_n(A,B) / R_AB^n * f_damp,n(R_AB)
42	```
43	
44	The exact parameters and damping variants depend on the chosen method. The
45	important data contract is that the contribution is signed: a stabilizing
46	contribution is not an absolute magnitude that can be added with a guessed
47	sign. The terminal energy of the program and an earlier self-consistent-field
48	summary need not have the same physical meaning when the pairwise term is
49	reported in a later section.
50	
51	## Parsing implications
52	
53	The output of a quantum-chemistry program is a narrative record of a
54	calculation, not a single table. The same calculation can contain several
55	ordered energy records, and different versions or calculation modes can print
56	the base energy, the optional contribution, and the terminal result in
57	different sections. A package-independent parser therefore has two
58	responsibilities:
59	
60	1. extract the scientific quantities represented in the supplied program
61	   family's supported output variants, keeping the contribution's sign and
62	   using the common unit convention documented by the package;
63	2. reconcile records that belong to the same calculation without silently
64	   changing ordinary calculations that have no optional contribution.
65	
66	The canonical electronic-energy convention in this source snapshot is eV.
67	The output files themselves commonly print Hartree values as well, so a
68	conversion must be applied consistently rather than comparing numbers from
69	different unit systems. A multi-step calculation must preserve ordering: a
70	correction associated with one record must not be applied to a different
71	record merely because both values are finite.
72	
73	## Offline investigation questions
74	
75	When reading the supplied output, distinguish the following concepts rather
76	than matching a single number:
77	
78	- an intermediate self-consistent-field energy;
79	- an optional signed pairwise correction;
80	- the terminal single-point energy emitted by the program;
81	- the normalized energy record returned by the common data model.
82	
83	The paper does not identify a source filename or a patch. The source tree and
84	the output must be read together to determine where the package currently
85	loses the scientific relationship between these records.
86
